findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Put both deprecated ids in the table (gpt-5.4-nano and gpt-5.4-nano-2026-03-17), each with its shutdown date, and state the match rule: strip the `openai-responses:` prefix, then compare exactly against the table.
evidence: 'from a module-level table citing the deprecations page (currently `gpt-5.4-nano`)'
Observation: page lists 'gpt-5.4-nano / gpt-5.4-nano-2026-03-17'
findings.finding: The deprecation-table match rule is unstated, and the table lists only `gpt-5.4-nano`, while the cited page also lists the dated snapshot `gpt-5.4-nano-2026-03-17`. Under exact-id matching, a future pin of the snapshot passes the test even though it is also slated for shutdown.
scenarios: Someone pins openai-responses:gpt-5.4-nano-2026-03-17 and the test stays green.
findings.suggested_fix: DEPRECATED = {'gpt-5.4-nano': '2027-04-01', 'gpt-5.4-nano-2026-03-17': '2027-04-01'}  # https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/deprecations, read 2026-11-11; compare model.split(':', 1)[1] for exact membership.

scenarios: The README nano line is deleted and nothing replaces it.
findings.suggested_fix: Add to AC 2: '...and `.github/llm-providers/README.md` names gpt-5.4-mini as the trivial-slot model.'

evidence: 3 criterion line(s) bundle multiple deliverables with 'and' (split so each is independently verifiable).

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Name the usage-log field that identifies the model class (or another trivial-specific marker) and assert at least one trivial-class entry with model gpt-5.4-mini and a success status.
evidence: 'it is already the arm's `standard` model ... exercised by every openai arm run since'
The plan names no usage-log field that records the model class.
findings.finding: The post-merge live check cannot attribute a gpt-5.4-mini call to the trivial class by model id alone. The `standard` slot already uses gpt-5.4-mini, so a usage log full of gpt-5.4-mini calls would pass even if no trivial-class call ran.
findings.location: Testing — 'check the openai job's usage log shows gpt-5.4-mini trivial-class calls completing'; AC 4 [non-codebase]
scenarios: The trivial path is mis-wired or never invoked, but standard-class gpt-5.4-mini calls make the log look correct.
findings.suggested_fix: In AC 4, require the recorded comment to cite the usage-log entries filtered by the class field (e.g. class == 'trivial'): a count of at least 1, model == openai-responses:gpt-5.4-mini, and every one completed. If the log does not record class, state which job step or test only issues trivial-class calls and cite that step instead.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] State how the live run's evidence identifies trivial-class calls specifically: either a usage-log field carrying the model class, or a named live test that routes through the trivial class. Require at least one such call to be recorded as completing.
evidence: "check the openai job's usage log shows `gpt-5.4-mini` trivial-class calls completing"
"recorded as a comment with the run id and the trivial-class call outcome"
"it is already the arm's `standard` model" — so the model id alone no longer separates trivial from standard calls.
The plan does not say whether the usage log records the model class, or which live test exercises the trivial class.
findings.finding: The live-dispatch AC asks for 'the trivial-class call outcome' and the Testing step says to check that the usage log shows 'gpt-5.4-mini trivial-class calls completing'. After this change, though, both the `trivial` and `standard` slots resolve to `openai-responses:gpt-5.4-mini`. A per-model usage log therefore cannot show that any completing gpt-5.4-mini call was a trivial-class call. The plan also does not establish that a dispatch of Live External Integration makes trivial-class calls at all. As written, the AC can be satisfied by standard-class calls alone, leaving the changed slot unproven.
findings.location: Testing (post-merge dispatch bullet) and the [non-codebase] Live External Integration AC
scenarios: The usage log shows gpt-5.4-mini calls succeeding, all of them standard-class. A trivial-slot misconfiguration (for example a typo in the overlay key) still yields a green-looking evidence comment.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a proving step: `git grep -n 'gpt-5.4-nano'`; every hit must be in the deprecation table or the documented deprecation history. State in Scope that this search was run and found no other files.

Scope lists only openai.toml, README.md, ci-provider-matrix.md and test_ci_provider_matrix.py.
findings.finding: AC 'no tracked file names `gpt-5.4-nano` as a current model' has no proving command, and it is a judgment a grep cannot settle. The new test's deprecation table and the docs' 2026-11-11 history entry must both name gpt-5.4-nano. The plan also never says the tree was searched beyond the four scoped files (e.g. other overlays, workflows, test fixtures).
scenarios: Another tracked file (a workflow comment, a fixture, a different doc) still presents nano as current and falls outside Scope.
findings.suggested_fix: Rephrase AC 2: '`git grep -n "gpt-5\.4-nano"` returns only the test's deprecation table and the ci-provider-matrix.md deprecation-history entry.'

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] In step 2, recompute the footnote's cost/usage estimate with gpt-5.4-mini pricing for trivial-class calls, or state explicitly why the figure is unaffected.
evidence: 'fix the estimate footnote's model list wording'
'`gpt-5.5`: the frontier model; a trivial slot gains nothing from it.' The plan weighs model cost for gpt-5.5 but not for nano versus mini.
findings.finding: Moving the trivial slot from nano to mini may raise the arm's per-run cost. The plan only fixes the estimate footnote's 'model list wording' and does not recompute any cost or token estimate in docs/ci-provider-matrix.md, so the documented figures may go stale.
findings.location: Approach step 2 — 'fix the estimate footnote's model list wording'
scenarios: The docs keep a nano-priced estimate while trivial calls are now billed at mini rates.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] State in the Root cause or docs section that the test only guards against known deprecations. Name the maintenance trigger (e.g. re-read the deprecations page whenever the overlay or the pydantic-ai pin changes) and record it in docs/ci-provider-matrix.md.
evidence: 'The overlay pins a model id with no check that it is still current'
'a module-level table citing the deprecations page'
findings.finding: The root cause names a missing currency check, but the fix only records known deprecations in a static, hand-maintained table. The plan does not say who updates the table or when. It also does not note that gpt-5.4-mini belongs to the same family whose nano sibling was just deprecated.
scenarios: OpenAI deprecates gpt-5.4-mini later; the table is not updated and the arm fails at shutdown with green tests.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] In docs/ci-provider-matrix.md, state whether the arm's cost estimate changes with nano→mini for the trivial slot, and recompute the figure if it was nano-priced (not just the footnote wording).
evidence: "fix the estimate footnote's model list wording"
"`gpt-5.5`: the frontier model; a trivial slot gains nothing from it" — cost-tiering reasoning appears for the rejected option, but the nano→mini step-up itself is not assessed.
findings.finding: Moving the trivial slot from nano to mini changes the cost and latency of every trivial-class call in the arm. The plan does not acknowledge this for the slot's callers or for the documented estimate. Step 2 only says to 'fix the estimate footnote's model list wording'. It does not say whether the estimate figure itself was computed with nano pricing and needs recomputing, or whether any budget or spend expectation for the arm changes.
findings.location: Approach step 2 (docs/ci-provider-matrix.md estimate footnote) and Choice of replacement
scenarios: The cost estimate in docs/ci-provider-matrix.md keeps a nano-priced figure while the footnote now lists gpt-5.4-mini, understating the arm's per-run spend.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Either reword the root-cause or fix scope to say the test guards only recorded deprecations, or name the process or owner that keeps the deprecation table current. Note gpt-5.4-mini's deprecation status and lifetime risk in the docs record.
evidence: "The overlay pins a model id with no check that it is still current"
"from a module-level table citing the deprecations page (currently `gpt-5.4-nano`)"
Choice of replacement does not address gpt-5.4-mini's own expected lifetime, given that its sibling is already deprecated.
findings.finding: The plan diagnoses the root cause as 'The overlay pins a model id with no check that it is still current'. Its fix is a hand-maintained module-level deprecation table that currently contains only gpt-5.4-nano. That table only blocks re-adding an id someone has already recorded. It cannot detect the next OpenAI deprecation, including one of the chosen gpt-5.4-mini, which belongs to the same 5.4 family that is now being deprecated. The plan neither names how future deprecations reach the table nor states that this residual gap is accepted.
findings.location: Root cause vs. Testing (a) / Choice of replacement
scenarios: OpenAI later deprecates gpt-5.4-mini. The table is never updated, the test stays green, and the arm breaks at that shutdown exactly as this ticket describes for nano.
